question: What is the primary focus of occupational health nursing?

options.A: Treating chronic community illnesses in primary health centers
options.B: Providing long-term bed rest for injured factory staff
options.C: Managing hospital budgets for emergency departments
options.D: Promoting and maintaining worker health and safety

explanation: The core mandate of occupational health nursing is keeping workers safe and healthy in their work environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h1)

question: How does occupational health nursing differ fundamentally from general hospital nursing?

options.A: It emphasizes workplace injury prevention over acute hospital treatment
options.B: It excludes any form of direct clinical assessment of workers
options.C: It deals exclusively with surgical procedures inside factory walls
options.D: It focuses only on administrative paperwork rather than patient care

explanation: Occupational health nursing focuses heavily on stopping workplace health hazards before they result in illness or injury. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h1)

question: An occupational health nurse acting as a case manager primarily does what?

options.A: Conducts financial audits for the company human resources department
options.B: Fills prescriptions for neighborhood residents outside the company
options.C: Purchases manufacturing machinery for the factory floor
options.D: Coordinates rehabilitation and safe return-to-work plans for injured employees

explanation: Case management in this context involves guiding an injured worker safely back to productive employment. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h2)

question: A worker returns to the factory after breaking a leg. Which nursing action fits the educator role?

options.A: Prescribing strong pain relief medications without consulting a doctor
options.B: Recommending immediate termination of employment for health reasons
options.C: Filing a formal disciplinary query against the worker for carelessness
options.D: Demonstrating proper use of personal protective equipment to prevent further injury

explanation: Teaching safe work practices and proper equipment usage directly reflects the educational responsibility of the nurse. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h2)

question: Which Nigerian legislation sets minimum standards for factory safety and worker welfare?
explanation: The Factories Act is the key legal framework governing industrial safety and welfare standards in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h3)

question: Why must an occupational health nurse understand the guidelines set by the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To negotiate annual salary increases with company directors
options.B: To design safe architectural blueprints for factory buildings
options.C: To determine the pricing structure for factory products
options.D: To ensure clinical practice remains within legal and professional boundaries

explanation: Professional regulatory bodies define what procedures and roles a nurse is legally permitted to perform. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h3)

question: Excessive industrial noise and extreme heat belong to which category of workplace hazards?
explanation: Energy-related environmental factors like noise, vibration, and temperature are classified as physical hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h4)

question: A nurse inspecting a hospital ward for needle-stick risks is primarily assessing which hazard type?
explanation: Infectious agents and body fluids present in healthcare settings constitute biological hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a pre-employment medical examination?

options.A: To determine the final retirement pension package for the employee
options.B: To replace the need for any future workplace safety inspections
options.C: To provide immediate treatment for injuries sustained during the interview
options.D: To establish a baseline health status before occupational exposure begins

explanation: Pre-employment checks record the worker's health condition before they are exposed to workplace hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h5)

question: Periodic medical surveillance is most useful for achieving which outcome?

options.A: Detecting early signs of work-related illness before permanent damage occurs
options.B: Eliminating all toxic chemicals from the industrial production line
options.C: Punishing workers who fail to wear protective gear on the shop floor
options.D: Calculating the daily financial profit of the manufacturing company

explanation: Regular monitoring catches physiological changes early, allowing timely intervention before severe disease develops. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h5)

question: Why is accurate documentation of workplace injuries essential for the nurse?

options.A: It replaces the need for any verbal communication with management
options.B: It supports legal protection, insurance claims, and preventive root-cause analysis
options.C: It serves as a daily entertainment bulletin for factory workers
options.D: It guarantees that the company will never face another industrial accident

explanation: Proper records protect both worker and employer legally while providing data to prevent future accidents. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h6)

question: An employee recovering from a hand injury is assigned to light administrative duties instead of heavy lifting. What is this practice called?
explanation: Modified or restricted duty allows recovering workers to remain productive without risking re-injury. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of applying ergonomics in the workplace?

options.A: Ensuring that all workers stand for the entire duration of their shift
options.B: Reducing the financial cost of purchasing office furniture and tools
options.C: Fitting the job and equipment to the physical capabilities of the worker
options.D: Increasing the speed of machine production regardless of worker fatigue

explanation: Ergonomics adapts the work environment to prevent strain and match human anatomical limits. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h7)

question: Which activity represents health promotion by an occupational health nurse?

options.A: Issuing a warning letter for reporting late to the morning shift
options.B: Calculating the quarterly financial bonuses for department managers
options.C: Organizing a workplace screening and counseling session for high blood pressure
options.D: Ordering new machinery parts from an overseas manufacturing supplier

explanation: Health promotion programs actively encourage healthy habits and screen for common chronic illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h7)

question: Under what condition can an occupational health nurse share a worker's medical record with company management?

options.A: At the end of every working week as a routine report
options.B: Whenever management requests the information for any reason
options.C: Only with the explicit consent of the worker, except in emergencies
options.D: Whenever the worker takes more than one day of sick leave

explanation: Medical confidentiality protects patient privacy, meaning employers do not have automatic access to private health files. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h8)

question: Why is 'dual loyalty' considered a major ethical challenge for occupational health nurses?

options.A: They must balance the health needs of workers with the economic interests of the employer
options.B: They must obey both traditional customs and modern medical science equally
options.C: They report to both the senior nursing matron and the chief accountant
options.D: They are required to work two different shifts in two different hospitals simultaneously

explanation: Dual loyalty arises because nurses are paid by the company yet ethically bound to advocate for the worker's health. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h8)
